design_detail: Cochrane systematic review with meta-analyses (update, pub2, of review CD015383; protocol published 2022) of psychedelic-assisted therapy against placebo or active comparators for anxiety, depression and existential distress in adults with life-threatening diseases. Randomized trials only; CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers searched on 30 March 2024 without language or date restrictions, with reference checking, citation searching and contact with authors and experts. Six crossover trials (149 randomized, 140 analysed), first-period data only: five of classical psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD), pooled, and one of MDMA (Wolfson et al., 2020; 18 participants), analysed alone. Risk of bias with Cochrane RoB 1; certainty with GRADE. This card concerns mainly the MDMA comparison. Funded by NIHR Cochrane infrastructure funding.
can_establish: What the randomized evidence up to March 2024 shows, and how certain it is, for MDMA-assisted therapy against placebo for anxiety, depression, quality of life and serious harms in people with a life-threatening illness: one small trial.
cannot_establish: Whether MDMA-assisted therapy reduces anxiety or depression in this population (one trial of 18, intervals including no effect), any effect beyond about a month (outcomes after crossover are uncontrolled), or rare harms.

sample.recruitment: Search on 30 March 2024 by the Cochrane PaPaS information specialist: 440 database records and 13 registry records, 304 after deduplication, 30 full texts; 6 studies (17 records) included, 6 excluded, 7 ongoing (Results › Results of the search).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Randomized trials (including crossover and cluster) of adults with anxiety, depression or existential distress (diagnosed or above questionnaire thresholds) and a life-threatening disease, any setting; interventions with a psychedelic at any dose plus preparatory and integration therapy; comparators placebo, active placebo or active treatment. The protocol's restriction to palliative care (more than 75% incurable) was changed post hoc to 'life-threatening disease' (Differences between protocol and review).
sample.demographics: Wolfson 2020: mean age 54.9 (SD 7.9), 14 of 18 women (77.8%), 15 White (83%); life-threatening cancer or non-dementing neurological illness, life expectancy of at least 9 months, STAI-Trait above 45; prior MDMA use 7 of 13 (MDMA arm) and 3 of 5 (placebo arm); single centre, USA, outpatients, 2015 to 2018 (Characteristics of included studies › Wolfson 2020). Across the six trials: ages 36 to 64, USA and Switzerland.
sample.attrition: Wolfson 2020: no dropouts at the primary assessment (12 of 13 MDMA participants after the open-label third session).
sample.selection_effects: All participants volunteered for psychedelic trials, many with prior use of the drug; most were White. PsycINFO was not searched. A registered randomized MDMA trial in anxiety with advanced-stage cancer (NCT00252174, terminated for lack of funds and participants) enrolled two people, both in its low-dose arm (ClinicalTrials.gov record read by this reader), so it adds no comparative data; the review does not mention it.

exposure.measurement: Wolfson 2020: two day-long blinded experimental sessions 2 to 4 weeks apart with nine 60- to 90-minute non-drug psychotherapy sessions (three before the first session and three after each), then an open-label crossover (Characteristics of included studies › Wolfson 2020).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions as printed in the review: by mouth, 125 mg MDMA followed by an optional 62.5 mg 90 to 150 minutes later; comparator 125 mg lactose (labelled 'active placebo group' in the table). The review's summary gives the MDMA range as 75 to 125 mg plus or minus 62.5 mg.
exposure.polysubstance: Concomitant opiates allowed; psychiatric medicines and ongoing primary treatment of the illness excluded (Wolfson 2020 table).
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Not applicable; primary outcomes about 1 month after the second blinded session.

comparison.controls: Wolfson 2020: inactive placebo (lactose) with the same psychotherapy; the five classical-psychedelic trials used low-dose psilocybin or LSD, niacin or placebo.

outcomes.instruments: Anxiety (STAI-T and STAI-S, 20 to 80; others planned), depression (BDI or BDI-II, 0 to 63; HADS-D), existential distress (Demoralisation Scale and others), quality of life, spirituality, treatment-related serious adverse events and grade 3 or 4 adverse events; two time windows, 1 to 12 weeks and more than 3 months after the intervention.
outcomes.validity_norms: Standard self-report instruments; for MDMA no existential-distress or spirituality measure was used. Quality of life in Wolfson 2020 measured with the Global Assessment of Functioning (independent rater) and FACIT subscales.
outcomes.operationalization: Mean differences of change scores from baseline, with standard errors computed assuming no correlation between pre- and post-treatment values, which widens the intervals (Methods › Measures of treatment effect).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None; GRADE certainty rated per outcome.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable. Selection, extraction and RoB 1 assessment by two authors independently with a third adjudicating; GRADE by two authors.

analysis.effect_sizes: MDMA (Wolfson 2020, 18 participants, 1 month after the second session): STAI-T mean difference −14.70 (95% CI −29.45 to 0.05); STAI-S −16.10 (−33.03 to 0.83); BDI-II −6.30 (−16.93 to 4.33); GAF 75.1 against 72.8 at 1 month (p = 0.52) and FACIT subscales (p 0.15 to 0.87) not different; no treatment-related serious or grade 3 or 4 adverse events; all very low certainty. For comparison, classical psychedelics pooled over five trials: STAI-T −8.41 (−12.92 to −3.89), STAI-S −9.04 (−13.87 to −4.21), BDI −4.92 (−8.97 to −0.87; 4 trials), SMD for depression −0.43 (−0.79 to −0.06), low certainty; heterogeneity low.
analysis.covariates: Subgroups psilocybin against LSD only (no difference); planned subgroups by number of sessions and medical condition not possible; fixed-effect sensitivity analyses gave the same estimates.
analysis.preregistration_detail: Cochrane protocol (Schipper 2022). Deviations reported: post hoc widening of the population from palliative care to life-threatening disease, first-period crossover data only, change scores, and other methods clarifications (Differences between protocol and review).
analysis.selective_reporting: None apparent; all prespecified outcomes are reported, including those not measured for MDMA.
analysis.power: Imprecision is the main reason for very low certainty for MDMA: one trial of 18 with intervals including no effect; the authors downgraded twice for it.

interpretation_gap.results_show: One randomized trial of 18 people with a life-threatening illness found point estimates favouring MDMA by about 15 points on trait and state anxiety and 6 points on depression, with 95% intervals reaching zero or beyond (computed conservatively by the review), no treatment-related serious adverse events and common transient side effects; certainty very low.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and conclusions describe the MDMA evidence as very uncertain and inconclusive, which matches the data. The Results text, however, states that anxiety and depression 'did not decrease' with MDMA, which reads an imprecise result as an absence of effect.

timeline.event: Wolfson et al. randomized pilot trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for anxiety with a life-threatening illness (Scientific Reports), the only MDMA trial in this review.
Protocol and first version of this Cochrane review (CD015383).
This update (pub2, 12 September 2024); seven ongoing trials identified, none of MDMA.

replication.where_it_stands: The highest-quality review of the question, but for MDMA it rests on one trial of 18 people; no further randomized MDMA trial in this population was published or ongoing by March 2024 according to the review.

funding.funder: National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), via Cochrane Infrastructure funding to the Cochrane Pain, Palliative and Supportive Care Review Group; no internal sources.
funding.declared_conflicts: SS and CB: members of the Swiss Medical Society for Psycholytic Therapies (SÄPT). KN: contract consulting for Acuta Capital Partners (discontinued). YS: research grant from the Swiss National Science Foundation. YB: research grants from Sunstone Therapies and Cy Biopharma, consulting fees from Reunion Neuroscience, unpaid advisory board member of Reset Pharma. GS: consulting fees from Roche. VP and ML: none.
funding.affiliations_note: The included MDMA trial was funded by MAPS and its authors received salaries from MAPS (Wolfson 2020 table). One of the review's clinical peer reviewers, Bessel van der Kolk, is an author of the second phase 3 MDMA trial for PTSD (author list of Mitchell et al., 2023, in its Crossref record).

what_would_settle_it: A larger randomized trial of MDMA-assisted therapy in people with a life-threatening illness and clinically significant anxiety, with a parallel (not crossover) design or a secondary open-label crossover, an active placebo, measured expectancy and blinding, existential-distress outcomes, and follow-up beyond 3 months.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: AMSTAR 2 gives low confidence when one critical item fails: here publication bias (15), neither investigated nor discussed. Otherwise the review meets Cochrane standards. For the MDMA question the flaw matters little, because the MDMA result is one trial taken from its publication, not a pooled estimate; that result is itself very uncertain. Cite the review for the MDMA trial's estimates as the review computed them (conservatively), for the absence of other randomized MDMA trials in this population up to March 2024, and for its certainty ratings.

key_findings.finding: Six randomized crossover trials, 149 randomized and 140 analysed: Gasser 2014 (12 randomized, 11 analysed), Griffiths 2016 (56, 51), Grob 2011 (12), Holze 2022 (20), Ross 2016 (31, 28), Wolfson 2020 (18 randomized and analysed); one evaluated MDMA (Wolfson 2020); USA and Switzerland; funding from organisations that promote psychedelic-assisted therapy, none from drug companies.
key_findings.locator: Results › Description of studies › Included studies, 1st paragraph; Abstract, Main results

key_findings.finding: Wolfson 2020: 18 randomized (13 MDMA, 5 placebo), single US centre, 2015 to 2018, outpatients; mean age 54.9, 77.8% women; life-threatening cancer or non-dementing neurological illness with STAI-Trait above 45; prior MDMA use 54% and 60%; two blinded sessions with nine psychotherapy sessions; funded by MAPS, authors salaried by MAPS. Risk of bias: low for sequence generation and concealment, high for blinding of participants, personnel and outcome assessment (more than 80% guessed their assignment correctly; outcomes mostly self-reported), low for attrition and selective reporting (primary outcome prespecified in NCT02427568).
key_findings.locator: Characteristics of included studies › Wolfson 2020 (study characteristics and risk-of-bias table)

key_findings.finding: MDMA against placebo, 1 month after the second session (18 participants): STAI-T mean difference −14.70 (95% CI −29.45 to 0.05); STAI-S −16.10 (−33.03 to 0.83); very low certainty (downgraded once for risk of bias and twice for imprecision).
key_findings.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › Entactogens (MDMA) › Anxiety; Summary of findings 2

key_findings.finding: MDMA against placebo: BDI-II mean difference −6.30 (−16.93 to 4.33), very low certainty; existential distress and spirituality not measured; quality of life not improved (GAF 75.1 against 72.8 at 1 month, p = 0.52; FACIT subscales p 0.15 to 0.87; 17 participants in the summary of findings).
key_findings.locator: Results › Entactogens (MDMA) › Depression; Existential distress; Secondary outcomes; Table 3 (secondary outcomes), Wolfson 2020 rows; Summary of findings 2

key_findings.finding: MDMA harms (Wolfson 2020): no treatment-related serious adverse events or grade 3 or 4 adverse events; no participant stopped because of side effects; MDMA against placebo: jaw clenching or tight jaw 11 (84.6%) against 1 (20.0%), thirst 11 (84.6%) against 2 (40.0%), dry mouth 9 (69.2%) against 1 (20.0%), perspiration 9 (69.2%) against 0, headache 8 (61.5%) against 1 (20.0%), lack of appetite 4 (30.8%) against 0, anxiety 3 (23.1%) against 0, nausea 3 (23.1%) against 1 (20.0%); reactions short, mostly resolved by the end of the session or within the following week.
key_findings.locator: Results › Entactogens (MDMA) › Secondary outcomes; Table 4 (adverse events), Wolfson 2020 rows; Table 3 (serious and grade 3/4 events)

key_findings.finding: Mean differences used change scores, with standard errors computed assuming no correlation between pre- and post-treatment values, which the authors note gives wider confidence intervals.
key_findings.locator: Methods › Data collection and analysis › Measures of treatment effect, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Classical psychedelics against active placebo or low dose (five trials, 122 participants): STAI-T −8.41 (−12.92 to −3.89), STAI-S −9.04 (−13.87 to −4.21), depression SMD −0.43 (−0.79 to −0.06), low certainty; no treatment-related serious adverse events.
key_findings.locator: Abstract, Main results; Results › Classical psychedelics; Summary of findings 1

key_findings.finding: All six trials were at high overall risk of bias because blinding could not be achieved; all were crossover trials, so only first-period data were analysed and outcomes after more than 3 months, all measured after crossover, have no comparison group.
key_findings.locator: Results › Risk of bias in included studies, 1st paragraph; Results › Effects of interventions, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: Seven ongoing trials identified (psilocybin, LSD, ketamine), none of MDMA.
key_findings.locator: Results › Description of studies › Ongoing studies; Discussion › Overall completeness and applicability of evidence, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: The protocol's restriction to palliative care populations (more than 75% with incurable disease) was dropped post hoc in favour of 'life-threatening disease', because few trials met it.
key_findings.locator: Differences between protocol and review › Changes to inclusion criteria; Discussion › Potential biases in the review process, 2nd paragraph

reporting_issues.issue: The Differences between protocol and review section says 'only four' included studies would have met the protocol's criterion but names three (Gasser 2014; Grob 2011; Wolfson 2020).
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Differences between protocol and review › Changes to inclusion criteria)
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the count or the list is incomplete.

reporting_issues.issue: The Wolfson 2020 characteristics table labels the comparator 'Active placebo group: 125 mg lactose', but lactose is inactive, and the Discussion counts four trials with an active placebo without Wolfson 2020.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Characteristics of included studies › Wolfson 2020, Interventions; Discussion › Quality of the evidence › Risk of bias, 2nd paragraph)
reporting_issues.consequence: The MDMA comparison is against an inactive placebo.

reporting_issues.issue: For classical psychedelics the depression analysis on the BDI is given as 4 studies with 112 participants in the abstract and summary of findings but 111 participants in Data and analyses (analysis 1.3).
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Abstract; Summary of findings 1; Data and analyses, Comparison 1, outcome 1.3)

reporting_issues.issue: Summary of findings 2 gives the placebo group's 'risk' as post-treatment scores (STAI-T 48.6; BDI-II 15.4) while the mean differences are of change scores.
reporting_issues.consequence: The placebo-group values and the differences are on different bases and should not be combined into an MDMA-group score.
